root_cause.text: In mm/__mmap_region(), the .mmap_prepare file-swap path updated map.file without mirroring reference cleanup on failure, so when mmap_zero_prepare() replaced desc->vm_file with a new shmem file and __mmap_new_vma() errored, the new file object was left without an fput().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states commit 605f6586ecf7 “handled the success path by skipping get_file() via file_doesnt_need_get, but missed the error path,” and the patch adds `if (map.file_doesnt_need_get) fput(map.file);` before abort cleanup with a comment explaining that only the original file was previously cleaned up when `.mmap_prepare` had set a new file.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the __mmap_region() abort path to release a replacement file set by .mmap_prepare and avoid leaking its reference.
intent_record.what: In the abort_munmap error path of __mmap_region(), a new comment and a conditional cleanup were added: if (map.file_doesnt_need_get) then fput(map.file) is called before vms_abort_munmap_vmas(&map.vms, &map.mas_detach).
intent_record.how: When mmap setup fails after .mmap_prepare has substituted a different file into map.file, the added code drops the reference to that new file during abort handling, preventing it from being left uncleaned while the original desc->vm_file is cleaned up separately.

vuln_statements.explanation: This abort-path return in __mmap_region() exits after failure without cleaning up a replacement file installed by .mmap_prepare into map.file/desc->vm_file. If mmap_zero_prepare() swapped in a new shmem file and __mmap_new_vma() then failed, this direct return skipped the needed fput(), causing the leaked file reference described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully present in this snippet of `__mmap_region()`, so it is sufficient to judge. The root cause was a file-swap path where `mmap_prepare`/zero-setup could replace `vma->vm_file` and on later failure the new file reference was not dropped. In this version, the cleanup path explicitly drops the current `vma->vm_file`: `unmap_and_free_file_vma: fput(vma->vm_file); vma->vm_file = NULL;`. This is important because the function also acknowledges that mapping setup may replace the file object: `/* ->mmap() can change vma->vm_file and fput the original file. */` followed by handling based on `vma->vm_file`, not the original `file`. Likewise, the shared-anon zero path uses `error = shmem_zero_setup(vma); if (error) goto free_iter_vma;`, and subsequent failures after such setup that route through `unmap_and_free_file_vma` will `fput(vma->vm_file)`. Therefore the vulnerable construct—updating `vm_file` without mirrored reference cleanup on failure—is not present here, and the fix is already included.
